root.name: Polish Opening: Rooks Swap Line
root.moves: 1. b4 e6 2. Bb2 Nf6 3. b5 a6 4. a4 axb5 5. axb5 Rxa1 6. Bxa1

overview: After 1.b4 e6 2.Bb2 Nf6 3.b5 a6 4.a4 axb5 5.axb5 Rxa1 6.Bxa1 the a-file rooks are exchanged. White is left with a bishop on a1 and a cramping pawn on b5, while Black is a pawn structure down in development of the queen knight. The game is quiet and manoeuvring.

white_ideas.idea: Keep the pawn on b5 and develop with Nf3 and e3
Use the long diagonal with the bishop on a1

black_ideas.idea: Develop with ...d5 and ...c5 and challenge b5 with ...c6

typical_structures.structure: Queenside pawn on b5 with bishops on long diagonals

character.notes: The rook trade removes tension and the game is manoeuvring.

gambit.notes: Material is level after the rook swap.

structure.notes: Flank structure with an undecided centre.

approach.notes: The Polish is seldom played by strong players.

character.reason: The rook swap leaves a quiet manoeuvring game.

gambit.reason: Material is level after the exchanges.

soundness.reason: The line is playable for both sides.

plans.reason: White uses the long diagonal and the queenside pawn.
